title: Blank Slate
statementMd:
Inspired by Piet Mondrian's colorful geometric paintings, Magikarp wants to turn his blank wall into a mural. He plans to begin with a large, eye-catching square. (He can worry about filling in the rest of the mural later.)

The wall is a rectangle $w$ units wide and $h$ units tall. Magikarp's square must fit entirely within the wall, with its sides parallel to the sides of the wall. It may touch the edges of the wall.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/be5157c20668f02d401b96b5b6e1ad1779197b46.png) Example of a Mondrian painting.

What is the maximum possible area of the square, in square units?

## Input

The first line contains two integers $w$ and $h$ ($1 \le w,h \le 10^3$) — the width and height of the wall, respectively.

## Output

Output a single integer — the maximum possible area of Magikarp's square, in square units.

## Note

In the first sample test case, Magikarp can paint a square with side length $3$. Its area is $3\times 3=9$ square units.

In the second sample test case, he can paint a square with side length $2$, giving an area of $2\times 2=4$ square units.

In the third sample test case, the entire wall is a square. Magikarp can use all of it, giving an area of $6\times 6=36$ square units.
